topic.title: Bayesian Optimization and Cost-Aware Search
topic.overview: Bayesian optimization chooses which expensive experiment to run next using a probabilistic surrogate of an unknown objective. This cluster studies local search, uncertainty, evaluation budgets, transfer between search spaces, and the cost of computing the surrogate itself. One representative method chooses a direction that maximizes the probability of improvement rather than simply following the expected gradient.
topic.whyItMatters: When each measurement requires a simulation or laboratory experiment, a useful search policy must spend both evaluations and computation carefully. Better uncertainty handling can make limited budgets more productive without assuming that a surrogate is perfectly accurate.
topic.evolution: The representatives span early density-based stochastic search through budgeted Bayesian methods to large discrete scientific libraries. Recent work allocates surrogate inference across molecular partitions using bandit policies, showing that screening computation has become an explicit optimization resource.
openQuestions: How should search balance surrogate computation, evaluation cost, and uncertainty when all three change during optimization?
